input: Build a command-line TODO app. Create /app/todo.sh that supports these subcommands: 'add <task>' appends a task to /app/tasks.txt, 'list' prints all tasks with line numbers, 'done <number>' removes that line from the file. Then demonstrate: add 'Buy groceries', add 'Write tests', add 'Deploy app', list all tasks, mark task 1 as done, list again to show remaining tasks.

transcript.final_response:
Created executable `/app/todo.sh` with `add`, `list`, and `done` subcommands. Demonstration:

```text
Tasks after adding:
1. Buy groceries
2. Write tests
3. Deploy app

Tasks after marking task 1 done:
1. Write tests
2. Deploy app
```
tool_calls:
mkdir -p /app
cat > /app/todo.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

TASKS_FILE=/app/tasks.txt

usage() {
  echo "Usage: $0 add <task> | list | done <number>" >&2
  exit 2
}

case "${1-}" in
  add)
    shift
    (($# > 0)) || usage
    task="$*"
    printf '%s\n' "$task" >> "$TASKS_FILE"
    ;;
  list)
    (($# == 1)) || usage
    if [[ -f "$TASKS_FILE" ]]; then
      awk '{ printf "%d. %s\n", NR, $0 }' "$TASKS_FILE"
    fi
    ;;
  done)
    shift
    (($# == 1)) || usage
    number=$1
    [[ "$number" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "Task number must be a positive integer." >&2; exit 2; }
    [[ -f "$TASKS_FILE" ]] || { echo "No tasks found." >&2; exit 1; }
    total=$(wc -l < "$TASKS_FILE")
    ((number <= total)) || { echo "Task $number does not exist." >&2; exit 1; }
    tmp=$(mktemp /app/tasks.XXXXXX)
    awk -v n="$number" 'NR != n' "$TASKS_FILE" > "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$TASKS_FILE"
    ;;
  *)
    usage
    ;;
esac
EOF
chmod +x /app/todo.sh
: > /app/tasks.txt
/app/todo.sh add 'Buy groceries'
/app/todo.sh add 'Write tests'
/app/todo.sh add 'Deploy app'
printf '%s\n' 'Tasks after adding:'
/app/todo.sh list
/app/todo.sh done 1
printf '%s\n' 'Tasks after marking task 1 done:'
/app/todo.sh list
